text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Kohl calls for a common fight against unemployment
- Justice minister proposes change in way sexual offenders are treated
- Bottle necks in food deliveries because of French strikes
- Four candidates compete to be craft workers' federation president
- Health insurance payments rise in third quarter of 1996
- Metal employers' association Gesamtmetall sees chance of settling dispute
HANDELSBLATT
- VW manager Lopez expected to resign on Friday
- Kohl offers in budget debate to cooperate with SPD
- U.S. inflation danger fades further
- Truck drivers' strikes block borders
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Kohl: Welfare state will not be abolished
- German-Czech treaty still expected in 1996
- Jail for Berlin child-porn producer
- President of employment office says jobless can be halved by 2000
- Forced labourers and other victims of Nazi regime from central and eastern Europe to receive one-off compensation
- Collapse in VW share price gets stronger
- VW considering short time work due to French truckers' strike and delivery problems
- Two billion overtime hours give room to manoeuvre for new jobs
DIE WELT
- Kohl looks for alliance with SPD
- Struggle over church language. Both churches facing problems over masculine language in services.
- Payments to doctors with own practices to be cut
- Werner Stumpfe warns IG Metall union against escalation
